entries.assessment_basis: Direct comparison against the authoritative 27 July 2026 consolidated EUR-Lex text demonstrated material article-level compression. Articles 4a, 9, 10 and 13 have now been re-extracted into 63 deterministic semantic-atomicity migration candidates replacing four coarse article-level abstractions; the remainder of the represented Act scope still requires the same review.
known_fidelity_gaps: The canonical requirements.json still contains the four coarse Article 4a, 9, 10 and 13 identities until the staged migration is applied and the full corpus validators pass.
Other operator-facing article-level records require the same semantic-atomicity review before clause-level fidelity can be asserted.

The 2026 amendment materially changes applicability and selected obligations; remaining records must be checked against the consolidated 27 July 2026 text rather than assumed unchanged from the original 2024 Act.
entries.next_action: Apply the staged Article 4a/9/10/13 migration, then continue re-extraction through Articles 11, 12, 14 and 15 and the remaining operator-facing provisions before specialist legal assurance and any fidelity-assured claim.

entries.assessment_basis: Direct comparison confirmed that the existing one-record-per-Core-subcategory approach follows NIST's source-defined outcome structure and does not require artificial sentence-level splitting for the audited sample.
entries.next_action: Retain current granularity; re-run fidelity review on material source revision.

entries.assessment_basis: Direct metadata-fidelity review of all 223 represented records confirmed that the source-defined suggested-action identities should generally remain stable, but 60 actions contain truncated or compound constituent semantics that are not yet explicitly represented outside compressed analytical prose.
known_fidelity_gaps: Sixty source-defined compound actions are recorded in reextraction-backlog.json for constituent-proposition preservation.
The existing action identity should generally remain stable while constituent semantics are enriched rather than mechanically split.

The source's AI Actor Tasks apply at subcategory level and are not action-specific; the metadata review preserves them as source-defined tags rather than attributing every listed task to every action.
entries.next_action: Enrich the 60 queued source-defined compound actions with explicit constituent propositions before restoring effective complete status.

entries.assessment_basis: Direct comparison with the CycloneDX 1.7 JSON schema confirmed three defensible ML-BOM proposition boundaries but found that the modelCard.bom-ref record combines mandatory uniqueness with a recommended reserved-prefix constraint and represents both as mandatory.
known_fidelity_gaps: EXTREQ-FA1B882FFAD54D93 requires deterministic semantic decomposition to preserve the distinct MUST uniqueness and SHOULD reserved-prefix modalities.
entries.next_action: Re-extract the modelCard.bom-ref constraints without allocating replacement identities during the metadata-review package; retain the other reviewed ML-BOM boundaries.

entries.assessment_basis: Direct field-level comparison of all 32 represented records against IMDA Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI version 1.5 found 20 records with section-level locators, over-compressed constituent practices, or analytical summaries that add or substitute source semantics.
known_fidelity_gaps: Twenty records are queued in reextraction-backlog.json; eight require semantic decomposition with identity migration and twelve require constituent enrichment or locator refinement while preserving identity.
The current catalogue uses section 2.2, 2.3 or 2.4 locators for propositions stated in narrower subsections, preventing deterministic source traceability.
Some summaries add unsupported scope, actors or outputs, including a generic required report where the primary text only calls for responsible human contact points.
entries.next_action: Re-extract the 20 queued records against version 1.5 with subsection-precise locators and preserve distinct modalities, conditions and outputs before restoring effective complete status.

entries.assessment_basis: Direct comparison of all 74 represented records against the July 2024 NIST SP 800-218A primary text confirmed that source-native recommendation and consideration IDs are generally defensible, but the source contains 75 distinct R/C propositions: PW.7.1 R1 and C1 were collapsed into one recommended-practice record, and five other summaries truncate source-relevant qualifications or constituent detail.
known_fidelity_gaps: PW.7.1 R1 and C1 require modality-preserving semantic decomposition with identity migration.
Five records require constituent enrichment to restore truncated conditions, qualifications, or source-defined examples while preserving their source-native identities.
The current canonical summaries and IDs remain unchanged during the metadata-review package; affected fields remain review-required.
entries.next_action: Re-extract the six queued records, preserving separate R and C modalities and full source qualifications, before restoring effective complete status.
